articles.title: Rafael López Aliaga a Jesús Gálvez: “Si quiere hablar, que no me bloquee (...) Estoy bloqueado por él”
articles.summary: El líder de Renovación Popular, Rafael López Aliaga, negó haber interrumpido el contacto con el tercer regidor electo de Lima por su partido, Jesús Gálvez, y dijo que es él quien lo mantiene bloqueado en WhatsApp. Sin embargo, justificó su pedido a Gálvez a para que renuncie a su militancia partidaria tras detectar aparentes contradicciones e irregularidades durante el reciente proceso electoral.
articles.body_text: El líder de Renovación Popular, Rafael López Aliaga, negó haber interrumpido el contacto con el tercer regidor electo de Lima por su partido, Jesús Gálvez, y dijo que es él quien lo mantiene bloqueado en WhatsApp. Sin embargo, justificó su pedido a Gálvez a para que renuncie a su militancia partidaria tras detectar aparentes contradicciones e irregularidades durante el reciente proceso electoral. “Para empezar, si quiere hablar, que no me bloquee (...) Le hemos enviado un mensaje ahorita y no hay manera que me responda. Le he enviado dos mensajes para hablar justamente y estoy bloqueado por él. Yo no le he bloqueado a él”, dijo este jueves al programa Beto a Saber de Willax TV. Acto siguiente, mostró su celular para mostrar que sus mensajes no eran recibidos por la otra parte. La declaración de López Aliaga respondió a las declaraciones que dio Gálvez en el programa “Siempre a las 8” de Jimmy Chinchay de El Comercio, en la que el también alcalde de Jesús María afirmó entre lágrimas haber sido apartado del partido mediante un mensaje de texto. En sus comentarios, dijo que se le pidió su renuncia sin oportunidad de dar sus descargos porque, según él, “había varios inconvenientes, hay información tergiversada que le debe haber llegado y que no hemos podido todavía aclarar”. Entre los argumentos expuestos, el dirigente enfatizó la postulación de Sergio Castromonte, excoordinador de proyectos de la Municipalidad de Jesús María bajo la gestión de Gálvez, a la alcaldía distrital de La Molina por una agrupación política rival. Según detalló López Aliaga, el candidato conocido como “el bombero” constituye un indicio de interferencia y respaldo a una candidatura que compitió de manera directa contra la postulación de Renovación Popular en dicho distrito. Un segundo cuestionamiento se relacionó con la falta de apoyo proselitista a favor del candidato distrital de Renovación Popular en Jesús María. Pese a que Gálvez ejercía como coordinador oficial del partido en esa jurisdicción, López Aliaga denunció la ausencia total de publicidad en este distrito. “En la distrital no ha habido un solo letrero, ni la cara ni el nombre del señor Lee, y el coordinador era Jesús Gálvez. Entonces le pregunto: ‘¿Por qué no ha habido un solo acto electoral, un solo acto de promoción?’. Cero respuesta, es lo que quiero conversar con él“. Asimismo, López Aliaga informó sobre la revisión en curso de cuatro contratos de iluminación ejecutados durante este año en el distrito de Jesús María. De acuerdo con el dirigente, las prestaciones de dicho servicio registrarían un presunto sobrecosto cercano a $1 millón. “Cuatro contratos que voy a investigar estarían inflados por casi un millón de dólares en Jesús María y que ese dinero habría ido a la campaña en La Molina, del ‘bombero’”. Finalmente, López Aliaga aseguró que el pedido de renuncia a Gálvez busca facilitar el desarrollo de las investigaciones internas sin incurrir en conflictos de interés. Añadió que la medida preventiva responde a un control de gestión posterior a los comicios para analizar el desempeño en cada circunscripción de la capital.

articles.title: A tale of two Nvidias | TechCrunch
articles.summary: We got two very different pictures of Nvidia — the company’s latest earnings report vs. the tech executives loudly calling for Jensen Huang’s return.
articles.body_text: We got two very different pictures of Nvidia this week, depending on whether you were focused on the company’s latest earnings report or the tech executives loudly calling for former CEO Jensen Huang’s return. On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Kirsten Korosec, Tim De Chant, and I discussed the latest news from the AI chipmaker, which reported soaring revenue and insisted that it has no plans for Huang to return. Kirsten described this as “the tale of two Nvidias this week,” with the company’s current executives assuring investors, “Hey, we’ve got this.” At the same time, “You’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back , circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back.” (The company’s falling stock price certainly suggests that Wall Street isn’t feeling reassured.) Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity. Kirsten Korosec: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China . This was coming directly from the interim CEO Colette Kress, and that coincides with the Trump administration also talking about closing off what we have discussed in the past, which is this idea of remote access — really closing and tightening all these restrictions [so] the chips can’t make it into China. What was happening is that data centers were being set up right outside, in countries like Malaysia and elsewhere, and then companies within China were remote accessing these chips, and so that’s now also been shut down. A lot is happening on the China front that is so much bigger than Nvidia, but Nvidia came out publicly and said, “Nope, we’re shutting this part down.” I’ll be very curious to see if this changes, maybe in the first half of 2027. Tim De Chant: I’d love to be a fly on the wall in some of these Trump administration conversations, because they were much more stringent in terms of export controls at the end of the first Trump administration, and that continued through the Biden administration, where they really restricted Nvidia’s ability to export chips to China. I think that something changed in the last couple of years that really opened Nvidia’s ability to sell in the country. Anthony Ha: One of the things that really surprised me as we were preparing for this episode was [learning that critics] of Nvidia’s stance towards China estimate that 20% of their business comes from China. And again, that’s not something you’re going to see directly in their financials, because that’s not direct sales to Chinese companies. But they’re saying, “A lot of the chips that are getting sold to companies in Malaysia or other companies in East Asia or Southeast Asia are going to end up [used by companies in] China eventually.” And so that could be — if Nvidia is really serious about this, I think this is something that’s very much in flux — that could actually be a pretty significant blow to their bottom line. Kirsten: Although Nvidia’s bottom line is doing just fine. In every possible way, their guidance was incredible. They beat expectations. They have a long pipeline. It was really interesting because you have that happening, and then you have all this noise happening in social media, and also a number of other tech conferences were happening this past week — Dealbook Summit, there [were] a few others in which you had the highest profile people that you can think of in the tech world commenting on Jensen [Huang], and Jensen himself commenting.

articles.title: Trump says reported FBI database hack is ‘not good’ | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The FBI is reportedly investigating a hack of the National Crime Information Center.
articles.body_text: The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), according to reports in CNN and the Associated Press . The NCIC is the online database used by federal and local law enforcement to share information about warrants, background checks, and more. The scope of the breach does not yet appear to be clear. A former FBI official told CNN that they’re not just concerned about “whether hackers gained access to sensitive information, although that is an issue, but whether they could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on.” President Donald Trump addressed the reports during an interview Saturday with Fox News, saying, “We just heard about it and I will say that it’s not good.” At the same time, Trump also said that as a result of the breach, “maybe we’ll learn things that we would have never learned otherwise because, you know, you had the Russia, Russia, Russia hoax.” In September, the FBI reportedly told agents and support staff that their personal information had been stolen in a cyberattack . articles.title: These desk gadgets can make your workday better | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The right desk gadgets can help you reduce clutter, stay focused, and add a little extra convenience to your day.
articles.body_text: We spend dozens of hours at our desks each week, if not more, so it’s worth creating a workspace that’s productive and enjoyable. The right desk gadgets can help reduce clutter, stay focused, and add a little extra convenience to the day. From ambient lighting to smart mugs, there are lots of products designed to make the time you spend at your own desk better, so we’ve combined a list of some options that we’ve tried and liked. Whether you’re working from home or in an office, these gadgets are worth checking out if you’re looking to transform your workspace. The Nanoleaf Pegboard Desk Dock is an interesting desk gadget because it’s three gadgets combined into one: it’s a customizable RGB light, a pegboard organizer, and a USB hub. It features hooks for hanging headphones, controllers, and cables, which can help keep your workspace clutter-free. You can also customize lighting effects and sync them with your music. It a great option for creating a clean and high-tech setup. The Elgato Stream Deck Mini is a customizable productivity tool that features six LCD buttons that can be programmed to perform different tasks with a single press. For instances, you could program it to control Zoom meetings, launch applications, open files, and manage music. It offers a fun and convenient way to simplify your workflow and create a personalized desktop command center. It’s currently on sale on Amazon for $49.93 . If your desk is cluttered with cords or a giant surge protector, Mount-It!’ s cable management tray is a great option for clearing up space. It mounts under your desk without drilling or screws, and it keeps cables and power strips off the floor and out of sight while still within reach when you need to plug something in. It holds up to 11 pounds and fits desktops from 0.2″ to 1.97″ thick. The tray is available on Amazon for $39.99. A monitor stand can help reduce neck strain by raising your screen to a more comfortable viewing height, so you don’t have to constantly look down while working. The Mind Reader Monitor Stand is a good option because it also features drawers you can use for storage to free up more space on your desk. If you want a tidier, more functional workspace, this organizer combines screen elevation and storage into one reasonably priced product. Who couldn’t use three drawers for essentials like stamps and perhaps a little candy bar to get you through the afternoon?

articles.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages | TechCrunch
articles.summary: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
articles.body_text: Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person. You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later. While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space. Below are the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work. Ask Proxy ’s biggest differentiator is that it “thinks like a woman,” meaning it aims to anticipate your needs before you even ask, the company explains on its website. It works like a chatbot you can text like a friend, whether you need gift ideas, help planning an event, or recommendations for things to do that weekend. You can ask it to add important dates to your calendar, set reminders, or help with everyday decisions. You can also send it photos, like an empty table, to figure out how to decorate the table for a dinner party. Unlike a typical chatbot, Ask Proxy also takes a proactive approach. It can reach out when it notices something you might forget or when it comes across a new activity, restaurant, or experience you might enjoy. There’s also a work-focused version, which the company explains “gets employees back to work faster, while keeping personal data off company systems.” The personal version costs $1 per day. For businesses, pricing starts at $15 per employee per month for large companies and $23 per employee per month for small teams with fewer than 49 employees. Ask Proxy works over SMS. You can text “start” to 820-732-2625. Caddy is an AI assistant that turns the information scattered across your phone into things you can actually act on. It lives in iMessage for iPhone users and RCS for Android users, so there’s no separate app or inbox to constantly check. For instance, an email contains an appointment that needs to be added to your calendar or a friend sends a list of things to pick up. Instead of worrying about all the details getting buried, Caddy connects to your calendars and conversations, then identifies things that may require action. It can add events to your calendar, set reminders, keep track of follow-ups, and even do research for you.

articles.title: Alaska, your next governor is a Wikipedia nerd | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, Alaska's governor-elect, has made more than 13,000 WIkipedia edits.
articles.body_text: We have arrived at a moment in American politics when people who are young enough to have grown up on the internet are being elected to office. That means there’s a lot more snooping into politicians’ online pasts to come. This month’s elections were no exception. Earlier this month, 37-year-old Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won the election for governor of Alaska , making him the first person to hold the office who was born in Alaska after it became a state in 1959. But when people went looking for more information about the Alaskan governor-elect, they didn’t find ill-advised tweets or compromising photos — they found out that he used to be an extremely active Wikipedia editor. On a Reddit page dedicated to discussing Wikipedia, someone posted that they had found what seemed very likely to be Kreiss-Tomkins’ account — a page for a user named Jonathan.s.kt from Sitka, Alaska who went to Yale, liked mountaineering, and made 13,358 Wikipedia edits between 2005 and 2011. The governor-elect is also from Alaska, went to Yale, and climbs mountains. Wikipedia editors are an impressive community: They keep one of the most important sources of information online (mostly) clean and accurate. This only makes Kreiss-Tomkins look better as a legislator. Check this guy out! A dedicated public servant to the global constituency of Wikipedia! But a moderator on the Wikipedia subreddit pointed out that we cannot be 100% certain that this account is his. “The odds that somebody would spend six years creating articles about Sitka, Alaska, Yale, and uploading PD photos of mountains, all to deceive people into thinking they were a disenchanted Howard Dean volunteer who was from Sitka, attended Yale, and was a mountaineer, is effectively zero. Plus they uploaded a photo of themself that looks like every other photo of JKT, minus the bald part,” one commenter replied. Fair enough. If someone created a Wikipedia account pretending to be some guy in Alaska, made over 13,000 Wikipedia edits, and then waited two decades until that guy became the governor of America’s 49th state in order to sabotage him by making him look like a conscientious denizen of the web, kudos to them. But I’m a journalist. I have literal nightmares about getting stuff wrong. If you’re not careful, it’s easy to get duped. So I emailed Kreiss-Tomkins, who is probably fielding many more important messages right now about policy, and asked if this is, in fact, his Wikipedia account. So, there you have it, people of Alaska — your next governor is a nerd. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Startup sues Apple in India over tap-to-share contacts feature | TechCrunch
articles.summary: A U.S. startup is seeking $162 million in damages and an injunction to impact iPhone and Apple Watch imports to India.
articles.body_text: Apple is being sued in India by a U.S.-based startup that alleges the iPhone maker’s NameDrop feature, which lets users share contact information by bringing devices close together, infringes its patented technology. GG Technologies, the startup behind StayTouch , an app that lets users exchange contact details by bringing their phones close together, is seeking ₹15 billion (about $161.86 million) in damages and an injunction against Apple, per court documents reviewed by TechCrunch. Santa Monica-headquartered GG Technologies filed the lawsuit in India in October after mediation proceedings initiated in April failed in September, the startup told TechCrunch. Pre-institution mediation is generally required before filing commercial lawsuits in India. The company also sued Apple in the U.S. in April over related patent infringement claims. In its 781-page court filing in the Bombay High Court, GG Technologies alleged that Apple’s NameDrop infringes its Indian patent on technology that helps phones exchange contact details with nearby devices without requiring manual pairing. The company launched StayTouch in 2019, the same year it first sought patent protection for the technology in the U.S. It filed its Indian patent application in 2021 and received the patent in July 2024. Apple introduced NameDrop as part of iOS 17 in June 2023. The feature debuted on iPhones later that year, with support for compatible Apple Watches arriving in October through watchOS 10.1. “We are seeking an injunction to restrict the usage of the NameDrop feature which is native to iOS,” GG Technologies told TechCrunch. GG Technologies urged the court in its filing to restrict Apple from selling or importing iPhones and Apple Watches preloaded with NameDrop in India. The case has yet to be listed for a hearing. In the U.S., the International Trade Commission opened an investigation into Apple’s alleged patent infringement in August, following a complaint from GG Technologies. The startup is seeking an order that could block imports of infringing Apple devices into the country, along with restrictions on their sale. Founded in 2018 by Gaurav Goel, a graduate of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi and a former Goldman Sachs investment banker, GG Technologies developed StayTouch as an alternative to exchanging business cards. The app is available on iOS and Android . Apple did not respond to a request for comment. India has become increasingly important to Apple, both as a fast-growing consumer market and a major manufacturing hub outside China . The Cupertino company has expanded its retail presence in the South Asian nation, where iPhones still account for less than 10% of smartphone shipments, giving considerable room for growth. articles.title: Experts warn: Nearly everyone in AI is susceptible to a honey-trap scheme right now | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Techies are building technology that can advance all aspects of the world — but can they protect their hearts? That's the vulnerability that honey pots exploit.
articles.body_text: Even as the fall-out for Nvidia over Jensen Huang’s alleged honey-trap scandal is still unfolding, Silicon Valley has yet to reckon with a new reality: many more people among them are at risk. “Nobody briefs founders on counterintelligence,” Aaron Brown, a former senior CIA officer and current founder of the software company Lumbra, told TechCrunch. That’s because historically honey traps have been associated with politicians, the military, and national intelligence — the people “behind clearances and a workforce trained to expect an approach,” from spies and other attackers. But now many of the most valuable secrets “sit inside companies building chips, models, and infrastructure,” Brown says, adding that a spy “wants what the CEO can touch. The roadmap, the export decisions, the customer list, who gets the technology. The CEO is the shortest path to all of it.” Huang has been accused of falling for just such a honey trap by having an affair with Alice Huang. She’s a former executive of a Singapore neocloud who’s been accused of being a Chinese spy and of smuggling billions of dollars’ worth of restricted Nvidia chips into China. After the Huang allegations broke, jokes flooded the internet about which tech CEO will be next, but it’s not just CEOs and founders who are at risk. The WSJ reported that OpenAI started warning its employees about outsiders trying to cozy up to them in search of company secrets. Anyone with access to sensitive information — from board members to executive assistants — can be the target of a honey trap. And typically, the attackers aren’t lovers. Friendship is actually the oldest honey-trap scheme around, Brown said. Honey traps gain access to their targets as investors, customers, recruiters, and consultancies. Their requests look legitimate on paper and don’t need their targets to fall in love. “They need you to feel comfortable talking,” Brown said. “They last longer because nobody’s looking.” What’s interesting, too, is the irony. So many tech founders are moving to automate and digitize so much of human life and yet remain vulnerable to the oldest bug around, a person who preys on the human need to be understood by others. “Why fight through a firewall when you can get close to the person who can open doors, influence decisions, or make requests nobody wants to question?” Perry Carpenter, a criminologist and chief deception strategist at KnowBe4, told TechCrunch. Once targets realize they have been compromised, the threat can escalate: attackers now have a means of blackmail. Another irony: AI has made honey-trapping much easier and cheaper. Planning a scheme used to take months or years of research, crafting a persona, knowing the target, and executing a plan. These days, it’s easy to use AI to research a target, generate fake social profiles, fake backgrounds, even fake voice calls.

articles.title: AI claimed a solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis — and a human did, too | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Mathematicians are having their minds blown by the latest AI-driven result — and there's a competing human solution, too.
articles.body_text: It’s a big week for Levent Alpöge: The mathematician saw his employer, Anthropic, become the first publicly traded frontier AI lab. He also appears to have solved one of the most important problems in mathematics. “The precise timing is horrible,” he wrote in an essay announcing his findings and describing how he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei last Sunday night to ask how to announce that he had found a Lean-compilable solution to the Riemann hypothesis, which dates back to 1859 and is among the Millennium Prize math problems. The hypothesis conjectures that there is a hidden structure underlying the appearance of prime numbers. If the claimed result holds true, we’re entering sublime-mysteries-of-the-universe territory. Maybe the best way to understand how exciting this is to the mathematics community is to watch the experts puzzling through the result in a chat on Zulip . Mathematicians like Chris Birkbeck, a number theorist at the University of East Anglia, are posting thoughts like this … The cohomology bound is proved by what looks like an automorphy-lifting argument. It genuinely uses the existence of Galois representations attached to regular algebraic, polarized cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n over CM fields, along with base change, Jacquet–Shalika, Clozel’s purity, Bernstein–Zelevinsky, the main theorem of CM, Deligne–Ribet and more. For my part, I tapped out of mathematics at college calculus, so I can’t help decode exactly what that means. But that comment was followed by 20 readers reacting 🤯. It will be a while before the mathematics community feels like it has a handle on the proof, but most appear confident that the formalized Lean result will hold. Lean is an an open-source coding language used to express mathematical ideas as code, allowing proofs to be formally verified. Several participants in the Zulip chat, including MIT mathematician Andrew Sutherland, say they have successfully confirmed that Alpöge’s solution can be compiled successfully. Alpöge appeared in his essay to feel a bit guilty about releasing the proof without a truly human-intelligible explanation, but his obsession with the problem since childhood made him feel he “could not live” if he waited to release the finding. Alpöge described a “stream-of-consciousness jaunt through the experience of finding all the pieces of the argument through incredible confusion with Claude” with more than a hint of AI euphoria, describing how the model “flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.” However, for all that action to mean anything, we’ll have to wait for humans to be able to understand the result and explain it to each other, something Alpöge has committed to pursue. Alpöge and a collaborator, NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster, also released another important proof related to the Navier-Stokes equations, problems that helped kick off the race between frontier labs and mathematicians to solve outstanding problems this summer.

articles.title: Bending Spoons buys Mailchimp for $3.68B | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Intuit acquired the company in 2021 for roughly $12 billion, so it looks like Bending Spoons is getting quite a bargain.
articles.body_text: Bending Spoons has bought up another distressed internet company. This time, it’s the email marketing firm Mailchimp, bought for $3.68 billion from the tax-preparation giant Intuit. Intuit acquired the company in 2021 for roughly $12 billion, so it’s taking quite a loss — and, perhaps, Bending Spoons is getting quite a bargain. At the time of the sale to Intuit, that acquisition caused headlines because Mailchimp employees reportedly received no equity, so no share of the sale proceeds, because the founders had allegedly promised them they didn’t need it as they would never sell. Flash forward to now, with Intuit hit hard by the Death Star to SaaS trade — aka AI — with the company’s shares worth less than half what they were a year ago. The company told Reuters that the sale will let it sharpen its focus on AI tools for small businesses, and the new cash will be used to repurchase shares. Bending Spoons describes the transaction as an all-cash deal, although that’s not quite true: As part of the same package, Intuit is buying $368 million in newly minted shares of Bending Spoons, so the net effect is a split of 90% cash to 10% stock. Still, the transaction is a major pickup for Bending Spoons, which has become a kind of clearinghouse for late-stage web properties, with its game plan to hold them long term. In just the last year, the company has snapped up AOL, Eventbrite, Airtable, and Miro . Previous acquisitions include older stalwarts like Evernote, Meetup, and Vimeo. In each case, Bending Spoons integrated the products into centralized engineering and revenue systems, resulting in significant cost savings while often improving the available support and product resources. “We want to place ourselves as an operator that takes beloved brands and makes them much better,” Bending Spoons co-founder and chief product officer, Matteo Danieli, told TechCrunch in July . articles.summary: FBI hackades återigen i veckan. Donald Trump reagerar märkligt positivt. – Vi kanske får veta saker vi inte hade fått reda på annars, säger han.
articles.body_text: Donald Trump reagerar märkligt positivt. – Vi kanske får veta saker vi inte hade fått reda på annars, säger han. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I september utsattes FBI för omfattande intrång som gav hackare tillgång till personuppgifter om tusentals FBI-agenter. I veckan var det dags igen. Hackare tog sig in i byråns centrala brottsregister. Angreppen kommer samtidigt som USA kämpar med en våg av driftstörningar i olika sektorer, där även banker utsatts för attacker, medan problemen i flygtrafikens datasystem ska ha haft andra orsaker. I en intervju med Kayleigh McEnany på Fox News – Trumps tidigare pressekreterare – ville Donald Trump anlägga en positiv synvinkel på angreppet mot FBI. – Jag gillar det inte, men kanske kommer vi att få veta saker som vi inte skulle få reda på annars. Vi hade ju Ryssland, Ryssland, Rysslandsbluffen, säger han. – Vi hade alla andra bluffar, vi kallar det Ukraina, Ukraina, Ukrainabluffen... det perfekta samtalet. Vi kanske får veta saker. Det finns så många andra saker. Det är inte sannolikt att intrången har någon koppling till utredningen om Rysslands inblandning i valet 2016, som inte var någon bluff. Därefter halkade presidenten, som så många gånger tidigare, in på sina lögner om valet 2020. – Vi kanske får reda på saker om valfusket, allt valfusk som genomfördes. Jag vill alltid ha en positiv vinkel på saker. Expressen erbjuder möjligheten att kommentera artiklar. Vi tar bort inlägg som vi bedömer är olämpliga. Kommentarer granskas inte i förväg. articles.title: Topparna vädjar: Låt Trump-eran vara över 2028
articles.summary: Desperata republikaner vädjar om att Donald Trump inte ska lägga sig i presidentvalet. Hoppet är fåfängt. – Låt Trump-eran vara över 2028, säger Charity Linch, partiets ordförande i Oklahoma.
articles.body_text: Desperata republikaner vädjar om att Donald Trump inte ska lägga sig i presidentvalet. – Låt Trump-eran vara över 2028, säger Charity Linch, partiets ordförande i Oklahoma. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Republikanerna slickar fortfarande sina sår efter den stora förnedringen de genomlevde i mellanårsvalet för snart tre veckor sedan. Samtidigt har blickarna redan börjat vändas mot nästa presidentval. Valet som verkligen ska markera slutet på Trump-eran. Eller? – Trump kommer att vara en del av det, vare sig vi vill det eller inte. Hans väljare är fortfarande de republikaner vi behöver få att rösta i valet om två år, säger Joseph Wood, ordförande för republikanerna i Arkansas, till Politico . Nyhetssajten har intervjuat ett stort antal lokala företrädare för partiet och alla är överens om att presidenten kommer att ha kvar sitt stenhårda grepp om partiet under överskådlig framtid. – Donald Trump kommer att spela den roll han vill spela. Han är president. Jag ser på saker som de är, inte som jag skulle vilja att de var, säger Mary Jane Truemper, ordförande för republikanerna i Nebraska. Men det finns gott om republikaner som nu öppet vågar säga att de vill att han håller sig borta, så att han inte sabbar partiets redan små chanser i valet 2028 ännu mer. – Jag vet inte hur mycket han egentligen har att erbjuda. Jag tror att de flesta är redo att gå vidare i en ny riktning, säger Paul Dame, ordförande för republikanerna i Vermont. – Han borde hålla sig utanför. Titta på de personer han gav sitt stöd till: de förlorade allihop, säger Michael Bub, ordförande för republikanerna i Taylor county i Wisconsin, ett starkt republikanskt fäste. Missnöjet med presidenten ses som den stora förklaringen till demokraternas förkrossande seger i mellanårsvalet, och enligt en mätning från Reuters/Ipsos i veckan fortsätter den negativa trenden. Bara 32 procent av amerikanerna godkänner hans insats som president och stödet bland republikaner har nu sjunkit så lågt som till 70 procent.

Det är nu upp till V att bestämma om de vill ta det eller förkasta förslaget, enligt uppgifter till Expressen. ”Går och lägger mig, utan att ha sett skymten av detta totalpaket till V”, skriver vice partiledare Ida Gabrielsson på X. Det uppger en C-källa med insyn för Expressen. Det är nu upp till Vänsterpartiet att bestämma om de ska acceptera budet eller förkasta det, enligt uppgifter. Vad budet innehåller är oklart. Vänsterpartiets pressekreterare Tommy Gabrielsson säger att de varken kan bekräfta eller dementera uppgifterna. Men på X skriver vice partiledare Ida Gabrielsson att de ”inte sett skymten av detta totalpaket till V”. ”Men Expressen verkar ha fått besked om det, till skillnad från V, vars mandat C, S och MP ju efterfrågar” , fortsätter hon. Gabrielsson skriver också att konstruktiva förhandlingar bör föras direkt med varandra i stället. ”Känslan av att det är ett blame game man sysslar med snarare än att faktiskt få till en regering, är svår att skaka av sig” , avslutar hon. Det har stormat inom Centerpartiet under dagen och flera tunga partiprofiler har uttalat sig om vilken väg de ska ta. EU-parlamentarikern Emma Ytterell, tidigare Wiesner, gick ut och sa att hon vill se ett samarbete med de tidigare allianspartierna . Centerpartiets tredje största distrikt, Västernorrland, gick ut med samma uppmaning till partiledningen. På söndagen ska det Skåne, som är C:s största distrikt, ha möte om regeringsfrågan, rapporterar Aftonbladet . Trots det uppges C nu ha varit en del av budet till Vänsterpartiet.

articles.body_text: En Uppsalapappa tröttnade på sin son – och drog honom till domstol. Nu ska sonen vräkas, skriver Hem & Hyra. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Pappan har länge tyckt att hans son borde flytta ut. Enligt honom bidrog sonen endast till mat och hyra under en kortare period. Pappan menar att den 23-åriga sonen borde ha pengar och möjlighet att flytta ut. – Han har jobbat tidigare och bor hemma. Han borde ha pengar sparade, säger han till Hem & Hyra. Nu läser han svenska på SFI för att sedan kunna läsa på komvux och i längden ekonomi på universitetet. 23-åringen säger också att det inte är första gången hans pappa vill sparka ut honom. – En gång låste han mig ute så att jag fick sova i tvättstugan. Det var för att jag inte lyssnar på vad han säger, säger han till Hem & Hyra. Pappan menar däremot att det inte stämmer.

articles.title: Brittisk by röstar för att lämna Storbritannien
articles.summary: I dag röstade Barnham för att lämna Storbritannien och bli självständigt. Anledning var hård kritik mot en ny plan för asylsökande män.
articles.body_text: I dag röstade Barnham för att lämna Storbritannien och bli självständigt. – Jag är verkligen tacksam för allas stöd, säger Helen Bock, ordföranden i boendeföreningen till BBC . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Runt 1 300 personer bor i byn Barnham som ligger i brittiska Suffolk – i alla fall än så länge. På lördagen höll de ett symboliskt val för att lämna landet och bli självständigt, rapporterar flera brittiska medier. Runt 500 personer var berättigade att rösta. 257 personer röstade för självständighet och 16 personer röstade mot, rapporterar The Guardian . Utropandet av den symboliska självständigheten är en protest mot regeringens förslag att inhysa 931 manliga asylsökande på den tidigare flygbasen i Barnham, skriver BBC . Röstningen är inte juridiskt bindande, trots det visade byborna upp sin nya flagga på en pressträff. En tjockfot-fågel mot en Suffolkblå bakgrund. Ordföranden i byns församlingsråd, John Bauer säger att byn nu kommer utropa sig till ”Barnhams bailiwick”, alltså ett självstyrande område, skriver BBC. – Samhället har slutit upp kring detta, och jag är verkligen, verkligen tacksam för allas stöd, säger Helen Beck, ordförande i boendeföreningen till kanalen. Regeringens förslag att flytta asylsökande till militärbasen har väckt starka reaktioner och demonstrationer i Suffolk. Boende i Barnham anser att det skulle göra byn överbelastad. Zia Yusuf, talesperson för Storbritanniens konservativa parti Reform UK, säger att röstningen visar att människor upplever sig fråntagna sitt inflytande i politiken. Barnhams socialdemokratiska parlamentsledamot för Labour, Peter Prinsley, blev inte förvånad av rösträkningen.
